title: Government Schemes and Current Affairs of Bihar

blocks.content: Government Schemes and Current Affairs of Bihar

Covers Bihar's flagship welfare schemes, most anchored under the state's long-running 'Saat Nischay' (Seven Resolves) framework — a fast-changing area, so treat the specific figures here as a snapshot and verify against the latest official announcement before an exam.

Much of Bihar's welfare and development policy over the past decade has been organized under the umbrella of 'Saat Nischay' (Seven Resolves), a flagship governance framework first articulated in the mid-2010s and subsequently extended into a second phase, spanning commitments across education financing, employment support, drinking water, sanitation, and infrastructure. Two of its most prominent and consistently tested components are the Bihar Student Credit Card Scheme (BSCC) and the Mukhyamantri Kanya Utthan Yojana, both of which have seen significant recent enhancements.

The Bihar Student Credit Card Scheme, launched in October 2016, provides education loans of up to ₹4 lakh to eligible students pursuing higher education, with a major September 2025 cabinet decision making loans effectively interest-free for eligible students (with some sources describing a differentiated near-zero rate structure for female versus male applicants), substantially reducing the financial burden on beneficiary families. The Mukhyamantri Kanya Utthan Yojana, meanwhile, is a broad girl-child welfare scheme combining financial incentives at multiple life stages — from birth through school completion and into graduation — with a specific, frequently tested component providing a one-time ₹25,000 cash incentive to girls passing Class 12 (Intermediate) examinations from the Bihar School Examination Board, intended to reduce female dropout and encourage continuation into higher education.

items: Saat Nischay is a broad governance and welfare framework encompassing multiple specific schemes across education, employment, water supply, and infrastructure, first launched in the mid-2010s and subsequently extended into a second phase ('Saat Nischay Part 2') with additional/updated commitments.

Key components under this umbrella include the Bihar Student Credit Card Scheme (education financing), the Kushal Yuva Programme (youth skill development), and the Mukhyamantri Nischay Swayam Sahayata Bhatta Yojana (a self-help allowance for unemployed educated youth pending employment).

The framework's broad scope means many individual scheme names encountered in current-affairs coverage of Bihar can usually be traced back to this overarching Saat Nischay structure, which is useful for organizing revision of what might otherwise seem like a large, disconnected list of scheme names.
Launched on 2nd October 2016 under the Saat Nischay framework, the scheme provides education loans of up to ₹4 lakh to eligible students pursuing recognized higher education courses across India.

A significant September 2025 cabinet decision made loans under the scheme effectively interest-free for eligible students, substantially enhancing the scheme's affordability compared to its original terms.

The scheme specifically targets students who would otherwise be unable to pursue higher education due to financial constraints, with particular emphasis on supporting female and differently-abled applicants through priority provisions.
Applications are processed through the official 7 Nischay/BSCC portal, with verification typically conducted through District Registration and Counselling Centres (DRCCs).

A comprehensive girl-child welfare scheme providing financial incentives at multiple stages of a girl's life — from birth, through various school-completion milestones, and into graduation-level education.

A frequently tested specific component: a one-time cash incentive of ₹25,000 for girl students passing Class 12 (Intermediate) examinations from the Bihar School Examination Board (BSEB), administered via the Medhasoft portal with Direct Benefit Transfer to the beneficiary's own Aadhaar-linked bank account.
The scheme's overarching aim is to reduce female school dropout rates and financially incentivize families to support girls' continued education through to graduation and beyond.

The scheme is administratively distinct from (though related in broad intent to) the Mukhyamantri Kanya Vivah Yojana, which provides separate, smaller financial assistance specifically for marriage-related expenses to BPL families, with an anti-dowry declaration requirement attached.
Mukhyamantri Mahila Rojgar Yojana — a flagship women's employment scheme launched in 2025, providing direct financial assistance (DBT) to support women's economic participation.
Har Ghar Nal ka Jal — part of the broader Saat Nischay infrastructure commitments, focused on ensuring piped drinking water access to rural households across the state.
Kushal Yuva Programme — a skill development initiative under Saat Nischay, aimed at improving the employability of Bihar's youth through structured training.

Given the pace at which Bihar's welfare schemes are updated (as seen with the September 2025 BSCC interest-rate change), candidates should treat this chapter as a framework for understanding scheme categories and always verify exact current figures, eligibility, and terms against recent official Bihar government notifications before an exam.

blocks.content: Table 9.1 — Key Bihar Welfare Schemes at a Glance

cells: Education loan up to ₹4 lakh; made effectively interest-free from Sept 2025
Multi-stage girl-child financial incentives; ₹25,000 on passing Class 12
₹5,000 (₹7,000 if registered) marriage assistance to BPL families' daughters
Direct financial assistance supporting women's employment/economic participation

Exam Tip

• The Bihar Student Credit Card Scheme's loan ceiling (₹4 lakh) and its 2025 shift to being effectively interest-free are both frequently and precisely tested current-affairs facts.

• The Mukhyamantri Kanya Utthan Yojana's ₹25,000 Class 12 incentive is the single most specific, most frequently tested numeric detail in this chapter — memorize it precisely, along with the distinction from the separate Kanya Vivah Yojana (marriage assistance).

• Organize your revision around the Saat Nischay umbrella structure rather than memorizing scheme names as an unconnected list — most individual schemes trace back to one of its component areas.
